# Core MVP Requirements Checklist: Ghaf Core MVP

**Purpose**: Review whether the Feature 002 requirements completely and unambiguously define the
competition journey, demo safeguards, and MVP scope before technical-plan approval
**Created**: 2026-08-22
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature
context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark
an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements
quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Complete Journey and Screen Scope

- [x] CHK001 Are the Parent-input, generation, Parent-review, Child-completion, Parent-confirmation,
      impact, and Ghaf-growth stages all defined as one complete journey with testable outcomes?
      [Completeness, Spec §User Stories 1–5, §Mission Lifecycle]
- [x] CHK002 Are the required inputs, state transitions, and outputs specified for every stage of the
      mission lifecycle? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008–FR-039, §Mission Lifecycle]
- [x] CHK003 Are exactly ten judge-facing screens enumerated with a distinct purpose and required
      content for each? [Clarity, Spec §Approved Screen Scope, §FR-003–FR-007]
- [x] CHK004 Are loading, validation, retry, error, and celebration experiences explicitly bounded to
      states of the ten screens, with scope changes requiring review? [Consistency, Spec §Approved
      Screen Scope, §FR-003, §Out of Scope]

## Arabic, RTL, and Visible AI Value

- [x] CHK005 Are Arabic and English requirements defined for every approved screen, mission state,
      and generated mission field? [Coverage, Spec §FR-017, §FR-040]
- [x] CHK006 Are RTL requirements specific enough to cover ordering, text alignment, logical spacing,
      directional icons, progress direction, mixed scripts, long labels, numbers, and units? [Clarity,
      Spec §FR-041–FR-042, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK007 Is AI value defined as a visible transformation of both the family message and the
      household food-waste situation into a personalized adventure? [Completeness, Spec §User Story 1,
      §FR-014–FR-018]
- [x] CHK008 Are the generated mission fields and the Parent review-and-approval gate defined
      consistently before Child assignment? [Consistency, Spec §FR-017–FR-021, §SC-007]

## Mock Honesty, Offline Fallback, and Reset

- [x] CHK009 Are real, mocked, seeded, simulated, pregenerated, optional-later, and future
      capabilities distinguished without contradictory claims? [Consistency, Spec §Prototype
      Capability Boundaries, §FR-002, §SC-014]
- [x] CHK010 Are the offline primary flow, optional-service failure, input preservation, and
      deterministic recovery requirements complete for the full journey? [Recovery Coverage, Spec
      §User Story 5, §FR-043]
- [x] CHK011 Is the ready-to-create reset baseline unambiguous about locale, role, empty draft, no
      pending submission, impact totals, streak, tree state, and the unassigned generation fallback?
      [Clarity, Spec §FR-044, §Mission Lifecycle]
- [x] CHK012 Is reset acceptance measurable across multiple source states and repeated trials?
      [Measurability, Spec §User Story 5, §SC-012]

## Approval, Impact, and Ghaf Progression

- [x] CHK013 Are mission-assignment approval and completion approval defined as separate Parent
      gates with unambiguous state effects? [Clarity, Spec §FR-021, §FR-028, §FR-030–FR-035]
- [x] CHK014 Are retry and repeated-approval outcomes defined so that impact, reward, mission count,
      and Ghaf progress cannot be awarded early or twice? [Edge Case Coverage, Spec §FR-033–FR-035,
      §SC-008–SC-009]
- [x] CHK015 Is food-rescue impact consistently defined as a Parent-confirmed estimate with a visible
      quantity unit, one record per approved mission, and no automated measurement or safety claim?
      [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, §FR-032, §FR-035, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK016 Are all six Ghaf stages and the requirements for below-threshold growth, stage crossing,
      and progress after the final stage explicitly defined? [Completeness, Spec §User Story 4,
      §FR-037–FR-039]
- [x] CHK017 Are the visible impact-and-tree response and milestone outcomes objectively measurable?
      [Measurability, Spec §SC-010–SC-011]

## Acceptance, Exceptions, and MVP Boundaries

- [x] CHK018 Are the approximately 90-second journey and judge-comprehension outcomes expressed with
      measurable rehearsal and observer criteria? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-001, §SC-013]
- [x] CHK019 Are missing media, denied permissions, interrupted generation, invalid quantities,
      language changes, incomplete submissions, repeated approval, uncertain food condition, and final
      tree stage covered as exception or edge requirements? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK020 Are the planning-only gate and MVP exclusions explicit and consistent with the
      real/mocked/later/future boundary, including no extra screens or production-scale features?
      [Scope, Spec §MVP Prototype First, §Prototype Capability Boundaries, §FR-047, §Out of Scope]
- [x] CHK021 Are minimum prototype safeguards documented for synthetic data, secrets, visible audio
      capture, Parent approval, food-safety claims, and nonfinancial rewards without expanding into a
      production security program? [Coverage, Spec §FR-010, §FR-029, §FR-045–FR-047, §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Independent requirements review on 2026-08-22: 21/21 criteria satisfied; no requirement-quality
  gaps found in the requested Core MVP focus areas.
- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify`
  and `$speckit-clarify`.
- Items assess the written requirements, not implementation behavior or test execution.
